title: Check inherited native-operation guards before adding wrapper validation
applies_when: A tensor-view wrapper uses torch.as_strided without an explicit raw-buffer capacity assertion and a candidate alleges silent storage-out-of-bounds access.
lesson: Test the actual pinned wrapper with real Torch before assuming as_strided is unchecked. PyTorch's concrete TensorImpl path calls setStrided, which checks the requested size/stride/storage_offset against storage capacity before constructing the view. Contrast an exact-fit control with an undersized buffer through the same wrapper; preserve the native exception rather than replacing Torch with a permissive stand-in. This can refute a missing-capacity-guard hypothesis without building a model or using a GPU.
avoid_when: Storage capacity is not the same as the wrapper's logical subregion or ownership boundary: a larger backing storage can admit a view that escapes an intended slice. In-bounds overlapping views, wrong offsets, unchecked custom kernels, meta/symbolic paths and other backends need separate evidence. A clearer public error contract may still justify wrapper validation. Do not treat this mechanism as proof that every tensor view or caller is correct.

evidence.note: checkInBoundsForStorage computes required bytes including storage offset and rejects a request exceeding backing storage. This is a version-specific native mechanism, not an application-wide safety proof.
The concrete as_strided_tensorimpl path invokes setStrided; Resize.h lines 184-203 in turn invoke the storage-capacity check. Meta and unchecked helper paths must not inherit this conclusion blindly.

Mamba conv and temporal views are created through real torch.as_strided. Absence of a wrapper assertion alone does not bypass the native check; logical subregions and valid caller invariants remain separate questions.
